description: Write a PySpark ETL script for fintech_app that applies a batch of change-data-capture records to an accounts Delta table. Each CDC record has an operation code (I = insert, U = update, D = delete) and a monotonically increasing change_seq. The script should: (1) drop exact duplicate CDC records, (2) for each account_id keep only the record with the highest change_seq in the batch, (3) MERGE into the target: I and U upsert the row; D performs a soft delete (is_deleted = true) and keeps the last known balance, (4) treat a U for an account not present in the target as an insert, (5) store last_change_seq and skip records whose change_seq is not greater than the target's last_change_seq.
edge_cases: a2 is inserted and deleted in the same batch: the D row has null balance and currency, so the last non-null values (5000, EUR) must be carried into the soft-deleted row
Duplicate delivery of a1 change_seq 2 must not cause a MERGE 'multiple source rows matched' error or a double apply
a3 arrives as U with no prior row and must be inserted
Replaying the same batch must be a no-op thanks to the last_change_seq guard
Ordering must use change_seq, never the arrival order of rows in the file
common_failure_modes: FM1: MERGE source not reduced to one row per key, causing non-deterministic or failed merges
FM6: Applying D by overwriting all columns writes null balance into the soft-deleted row
FM7: No guard on last_change_seq, so a replayed older batch reverts newer state
